## Purpose, in one line each

- **`filmopen_account`** — The filmopen.ai account: sign-in through Supabase with PKCE (`account_auth.dart`), the `ai.filmopen.desktop://` callback registration (Windows; a phone's scheme is in its manifest) and the callback's arrival through the platform's link d…
- **`filmopen_assistant_ui`** — Reusable field-assistant controls, with session contracts supplied by `filmopen_state`.
- **`filmopen_automation`** — The agent layer's in-app half (the MCP Specification): Flutter's driver extension, the protocol of its data channel, and the host that answers it.
- **`filmopen_browser`** — The pages: the browser page with the tree pane and the detail pane, the entity page (header, version row, tabs: the form, Script, Workflow, Compare, Takes, Commentary), the epoch overview (a character's cards listing its outfits at each…
- **`filmopen_cloud`** — Pure Dart FilmOpen Cloud client and `FilmOpenCloudTarget`, implementing the same `SyncTarget` contract as Drive and folders. It depends on the format, sync, store and HTTP packages, its tests on crypto too; it draws no UI and imports no…
- **`filmopen_compare`** — Compare: the same form twice, one field per row, the viewer's latest on the left and the selected version on the right, with copy-left on the split — `<` per row, `<<` per section, `<<<` in the header — through the left column's autosave…
- **`filmopen_comps`** — Prepare a comp — a standalone comparison of renders — from caller JSON and local originals, then publish its immutable bundle through the comps publishing contract `/v1` (`packages/comps/openapi/publishing.yaml` in filmopen-web, summariz…
- **`filmopen_device`** — The device's identity (Software Specification §6.6b): a **P-256 key pair** the installation makes the first time it registers, its private half kept in the device's credential store (`CredentialStore.current` — DPAPI, the Keychain, the K…
- **`filmopen_dictation`** — Dictation on a text box, as Software Specification §9.6 describes it.
- **`filmopen_drive`** — Google sign-in, the Drive HTTP client and a resumable target for sharing a film. The application's root package does not import it — `filmopen_sharing` does — and Drive is never a media root. The package has no media store, source panel,…
- **`filmopen_engine`** — The timeline engine interface as pure Dart (Software Specification §19): `EngineTimeline` — one flat, fully resolved timeline with its tracks, items and markers, its JSON (`timeline.dart`) and `validate()`'s codes —, the one frame arithm…
- **`filmopen_engine_android`** — An Android-only `TimelineEngine` using Media3 `CompositionPlayer` on Flutter's `SurfaceProducer`. It plays clips, sounds and scene compositions: trimmed videos, stills and black, with an extracted last-frame hold beyond a video's source,…
- **`filmopen_engine_bench`** — The timeline engines' bench (Software Specification §19.11): a Flutter app for Linux and Windows that drives any `TimelineEngine`, wrapped in `LoggingEngine`, through the fixture scene of `scripts/make_timeline_fixture.py` and writes `be…
- **`filmopen_engine_mlt`** — Prototype A of the timeline engine (Software Specification §19): MLT behind `filmopen_engine`'s `TimelineEngine`, as a Flutter plug-in for Linux and Windows.
- **`filmopen_engine_mpv`** — Pure compilers translate an `EngineTimeline` into an mpv EDL loaded through `memory://` and an FFmpeg export command. The picture, clip sound and audio lanes use the same frame boundaries and gains. Audio gaps are explicit silence; the m…
- **`filmopen_exchange`** — Pure Dart vocabulary for exchanging FilmOpen content: ids, field paths, projections and the `$` key codec. The public API is exported through `filmopen_exchange.dart`.
- **`filmopen_fdx`** — A pure Dart screenplay importer. `importScriptFile(path, author:, epochLabel:)` reads a bounded local file in an isolate and returns a `ScriptImportResult`: its in-memory source, project version and warning codes. Content selects the rea…
- **`filmopen_format`** — The FilmOpen file format as pure Dart, and nothing else: the filename grammar (`stems.dart`), documents (`entity.dart`), the index and resolution — `resolve`, `pickAt`, `nameOf`, `forViewer` — (`project.dart`), epochs, kinds, character a…
- **`filmopen_forms`** — One form per type in two modes — *Edit* on the viewer's own writable version, *View*, the same boxes locked, on any other (`entity_form.dart`, the type→form door `entity_data_spec.dart`, the per-type tabs — the project's (its subtitle fo…
- **`filmopen_insertion`** — Media insertion, separate from storage and playback. This pure Dart package may depend on `filmopen_jobs`, `filmopen_media`, `filmopen_store` and `filmopen_format`, through their public barrels. It imports no state, forms, plug-in host o…
- **`filmopen_insertion_ui`** — The media place: one element for every place a film keeps media (Software Specification §9.3).
- **`filmopen_jobs`** — Application-owned jobs, persistence and scheduling, independent of the film and its screens.
- **`filmopen_jobs_ui`** — How a job looks: one row for a `JobView` — its name, its sentence, its progress and its actions — and two pages of the rail: *Activity*, which shows this device's usage (a section the application hands in as a builder, since this package…
- **`filmopen_js`** — QuickJS-NG, bound for one call at a time. It knows nothing of FilmOpen: the plug-in host (`filmopen_plugin_host`) gives it a script, a function name, JSON arguments and the data `ctx` is built from, and answers the script's requests thro…
- **`filmopen_keys`** — The key cards (Software Specification §6.7, §9.4): `KeyCards(owner:)` draws an enabled plug-in's own key slots on its page under Settings → Plugins, where a user stores a key, checks it with the platform and removes it. Every key belongs…
- **`filmopen_l10n`** — Every user-facing string of FilmOpen, **one ARB file per language** (`lib/l10n/app_en.arb`, `app_es.arb`), the generated `AppLocalizations`, and `labels.dart`, which turns the format's codes (warning kinds, account problems, field names)…
- **`filmopen_machine`** — This computer's OS, CPU, RAM and GPU memory facts, read once per session. Linux uses local standard sources and nvidia-smi; Windows reads its GPUs alone with the same nvidia-smi query, found on the PATH where NVIDIA's driver put it, and…
- **`filmopen_mcp`** — The MCP server for FilmOpen (the MCP Specification). It is a Dart command-line program that an agent's MCP client spawns, and it drives a running FilmOpen agent build through Flutter's driver extension. The MCP library (`dart_mcp`) lives…
- **`filmopen_media`** — Local media storage, playback values and input descriptions.
- **`filmopen_media_ui`** — Media tiles and their provenance, the file dialog by kind, the viewer and the platform player.
- **`filmopen_picker`** — The prompt-builder picker: its model — resolved catalogs, deferred pictures, stored choices and prompt lookup through the plug-in seam — and its widgets.
- **`filmopen_platform`** — Where the application meets the operating system and the bundle: the bundled sample and the seed library as a `ProjectSource` (`asset_source.dart`), the on-disk copy of bundled assets, the application's own folders (`app_paths*.dart`: lo…
- **`filmopen_plugin_dev`** — The plug-in developer page: a link for a person who writes plug-ins, never for one who only uses them. It reads a plug-in's files again from disk, offers what it exposes in the interface definition's terms — `status` first — and runs a c…
- **`filmopen_plugin_host`** — The plug-in runtime (Software Specification §6.11): the registry of plug-ins in the development folder and shared library, the stock install from the app's bundle, trust and consent, grants, preferred providers, machine settings and stor…
- **`filmopen_plugins`** — What a FilmOpen plug-in is, as pure Dart: the manifest and its schemas (`plugin_manifest.dart`, `setting_spec.dart`), key ids and their store names (`key_id.dart`), **the interface definition read** (`plugin_api.dart`: `PluginApi`, from…
- **`filmopen_plugins_ui`** — Settings → Plugins (Software Specification §9.4): the list of plug-ins, a tree by what their manifests name in `x.dependencies`, with *Install from file…* and the preferred providers, the consent screen, and a plug-in's page — its switch…
- **`filmopen_prompt_ui`** — The Prompt card (Software Specification §9.3): one prompt of a document (Project Specification §9.0) as a card of its own, on every editor that holds a prompt. It sits below its three consumers, `filmopen_forms`, `filmopen_render_ui` and…
- **`filmopen_recorder`** — The issue recorder (Software Specification §6.8). While `Recorder.instance` records, every tap, drag, scroll, key, typed text, draft change, navigation, tab, route, setting and log event goes into `tape.jsonl`, with a JPEG of the whole v…
- **`filmopen_relay`** — *Remote control* (Software Specification §6.6c): the one socket this device holds to filmopen.ai's relay, `wss://<kFilmOpenDomain>/v1/relay/socket`, so that the person's chat app reaches this device's commands through the website, and a…
- **`filmopen_render`** — Renders asked for anywhere in the application, run in one queue that needs no film (Software Specification §6.15). Pure Dart: it depends on `filmopen_jobs` and `filmopen_format` and nothing else of FilmOpen, and imports no Flutter and no…
